correctness.rationale: A surviving five-bit word is a distinct arc from its four-bit prefix to its four-bit suffix. Cyclic factor overlap is exactly a closed edge traversal; conversely reading the appended bits of an Euler circuit recovers the retained factors. Degree balance plus weak connectivity on active vertices is the Euler criterion, with the length ≥5 requirement imposed separately. The full graph is balanced, so deletion and retention balance are equivalent, including the two loops. An independent enumerator joins on consistent vertex-local assignments of 0/1 retention variables, with one occurrence per globally balanced mask, then constructs a Hierholzer tour and checks the actual cyclic five-factors whenever the tour uses every eligible edge. It matches every b_s and c_s in the frozen table; the balanced total is 6600. At s=27, the prime length five leaves precisely the six nonconstant primitive rotation classes (32−2)/5; no candidate of smaller length qualifies. Uniform labeled deletion sets give the binomial denominator.
residual_risks: Exhaustive exact computation for this fixed graph, not a formula for other orders. The original scripts were inspected but not executed.
